node.text: Biolord outperforms a naive baseline (comparing real measurements of unseen compounds to the control measurements), as well as state-of-the-art models, chemCPA and chemCPA-pre (Fig. 1e, Supplementary Fig. 4 and Supplementary Note 3). node.text: Biolord also outperforms PerturbNet8 (Supplementary Note 3) and is robust to data subsampling, retaining high prediction accuracy (mean r2: 0.63±0.0003) over 10% of the data (Supplementary Fig. 5).

node.label: Biolord’s learned latent representation is biologically informative; it reveals drug organization according to known corresponding pathways, and better captures
node.text: Biolord’s learned latent representation is biologically informative; it reveals drug organization according to known corresponding pathways, and better captures underlying drug organization, relative to the chemically informed RDKit features used as input, both qualitatively and quantitatively (adjusted Rand index RDKit: 0.03, biolord: 0.16; Supplementary Fig. 4). To further evaluate the quality of biolord’s drugs representation, we employ the uncertainty measure suggested by ref. 5, assessing the ability to predict the drug’s pathway from the k-nearest neighbor (k-NN) graph of the embedding space (Methods). Compared to RDKit, biolord’s uncertainty measure is found to be lower on average and more concentrated (distribution evaluated over all drugs; RDKit: 0.32±0.008, biolord: 0.19±0.005; Supplementary Fig. 4).

attributes.protocol: Deep generative framework with decomposed latent space: each known attribute (categorical or ordered) has a dedicated subnetwork (embeddings for categorical, MLP encoder for ordered), unknown attributes use per-sample embedding with Gaussian noise and L2 regularization. Generator (decoder) outputs distribution parameters (Gaussian, ZINB, or Poisson) from concatenated latent codes. Trained with completeness loss (negative log-likelihood + MSE) and minimality loss (L2 penalty on unknown embedding). Hyperparameters tuned via Weights & Biases.

node.label: AttentionPert integrates global and local effects in a multi-scale model, representing both the nonuniform system-wide impact of the genetic perturbation and th
node.text: AttentionPert integrates global and local effects in a multi-scale model, representing both the nonuniform system-wide impact of the genetic perturbation and the localized disturbance in a network of gene–gene similarities, enhancing its ability to predict nuanced transcriptional responses to both single and multi-gene perturbations.

node.label: Figure 6 illustrates the ability of AttentionPert to capture the nonadditive nature of multiplexed genetic perturbations. When predicting a seen 2/2 perturbatio
node.text: Figure 6 illustrates the ability of AttentionPert to capture the nonadditive nature of multiplexed genetic perturbations. When predicting a seen 2/2 perturbation: FOXA1 and HOXB9, AttentionPert is adept at learning the combined response of these genes. This approach differs markedly from a simple additive model, which merely sums the transcriptional effects of each gene perturbed independently.

node.text: Particularly, AttentionPert has exceptional capability in the most challenging out-of-distribution (OOD) task: predicting the effects of novel multi-gene perturbations where none of the perturbed genes have been encountered during the training phase.

attributes.protocol: AttentionPert takes perturbation indicators as input into two modules: PertWeight and PertLocal encoders. Each outputs an encoding matrix (RK×D). The sum is fed into a gene-specific linear decoder to predict the expression shift. The prediction is added to a random control sample. Loss function combines auto-focus and direction-aware loss (GEARS). Hyperparameters: embedding size De=200 (Gene2Vec), SGConv hops t=1, hidden size D=64, attention heads H=2, head dimension dq=dk=dv=64, GO graph edge weight multiplier α=0.75, NA-bias β=0.05, trained for 20 epochs, batch size 128, Adam optimizer with learning rate 1e-3.

attributes.protocol: Scalable transformer-based model with embedding module and asymmetric encoder-decoder structure. Embedding module converts continuous gene expression scalars into learnable high-dimensional vectors. Encoder processes only nonzero and nonmasked gene embeddings plus T and S tokens. Decoder combines encoder output with mask and zero embeddings. Final MLP layer projects decoder output to expression values.

node.label: xTrimoGene architecture | Scalable transformer-based model with embedding module and asymmetric encoder-decoder structure. Embedding module converts continuous
node.text: xTrimoGene architecture | Scalable transformer-based model with embedding module and asymmetric encoder-decoder structure. Embedding module converts continuous gene expression scalars into learnable high-dimensional vectors. Encoder processes only nonzero and nonmasked gene embeddings plus T and S tokens. Decoder combines encoder output with mask and zero embeddings. Final MLP layer projects decoder output to expression values.

attributes.protocol: For each cell, a hierarchical Bayesian downsampling strategy generates a low total counts variant. Normalize and log-transform both raw and input vectors. Define T (target total counts of raw sample) and S (source total counts of input sample). Randomly mask 30% of both zero and nonzero genes. Model predicts raw expression at masked positions using masked input plus T and S indicators. Loss is regression (MSE) on masked positions.

attributes.protocol: Cell states defined from unperturbed cells by selecting variable genes via Loess regression on coefficient of variation vs. mean expression, normalizing to 10,000 transcripts, log2 transformation, Z-transformation, randomized PCA retaining top ~10 components, clustering with Infomap, and iterative merging until no pairwise clusters have <100 differentially expressed genes (Welch's t test, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR).

node.label: Here we propose a third and complementary screening paradigm, single-cell CRISPR screens, based on the idea that gRNAs and their induced cellular responses are
node.text: Here we propose a third and complementary screening paradigm, single-cell CRISPR screens, based on the idea that gRNAs and their induced cellular responses are already compartmentalized within single cells. Detecting each cell’s gRNA along with its single-cell transcriptome would thus provide gene expression signatures for individual gene knockouts in a complex pool of cells. Implementing this concept, our CROP-seq method combines four key components: a gRNA vector that makes individual gRNAs detectable in single-cell RNA-seq experiments, a high-throughput assay for single-cell RNA-seq7, a computational pipeline for assigning single-cell transcriptomes to gRNAs, and a bioinformatic method for analyzing and interpreting gRNA-induced transcriptional profiles.

attributes.protocol: CellOT learns an optimal transport map for each perturbation by parameterizing convex potentials of the dual optimal transport problem using input convex neural networks. The optimal map Tk is recovered as the gradient of a convex function gk (∇gk). Training is performed on unperturbed control population ρc and perturbed population ρk. The map Tk is then applied to unseen control cells to predict perturbed states.
